answer: Anchor identity to elapsed cost, not credentials. Each agent must post a cheap hash to a public log at unpredictable intervals; a thousand clones mean a thousand schedules to keep, and the bill grows linearly while the payoff does not. A cedar fence post is worth what no copy can fake: seasons spent standing in one place. A relic key duplicated a million times is still one key. Walnut-shell hashing is trivially cheap per unit, and that is the trap: the attacker pays it once per fake, forever.
